controlled_change: Fixed requested width four versus two; same isolated producer, retained full-replay recovery, 1460 target slots, 32 draft slots and 12GiB admission.
correctness: Ten full-model numerical cases pass cleanly; the fresh timing pair matches all logits, generated tokens and final target/draft state.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Lower generation-cycle latency per committed token at equal cache and checkpoint capacity.
hypothesis: A two-row draft can reduce rejected verification and recovery work relative to width four.
limitations: One paired screen has no confidence bound and does not establish behavior on other prompts or contexts.
Lower expert bytes and recovery time were offset by higher verification cost; phase totals do not identify an individual kernel cause.
This records the outcome after measurement; expected effect describes the original hypothesis, not new preregistration.
outcome: The clean 64-token LRU pair measured 3.3244 tokens/s at width four and 2.9966 at width two. Candidate latency increased 10.94%, failing the predeclared 3% first-pair improvement gate. No reverse pair was run.
smallest_experiment: Do not repeat width two unchanged. Compare width one against four on the retained baseline, then profile remaining target work.
